definition: Casual or unconstrained conversation about other people, typically involving details that are not confirmed as true
etymology: From Old English 'godsibb' (godparent), which evolved to mean a close friend one gossips with, then the act of gossiping itself
contextSentence: First, gossip. Speaking ill of somebody who's not present.
contextSentenceKo: 첫째, 험담. 자리에 없는 사람을 나쁘게 말하는 것입니다.

definition: The tendency to lay down principles as incontrovertibly true, without consideration of evidence or the opinions of others
etymology: From Greek 'dogma' (opinion, tenet), from 'dokein' (to seem, to think)
contextSentence: And finally, dogmatism. The confusion of facts with opinions.
contextSentenceKo: 그리고 마지막으로, 독단주의. 사실과 의견을 혼동하는 것입니다.

definition: To combine two or more things, especially texts or ideas, into one, often mistakenly treating them as equivalent
meaningKo: 혼동하다, 합치다 (특히 별개의 것을 하나로 섞어버리다)
etymology: From Latin 'conflare' (to blow together), from 'con-' (together) + 'flare' (to blow)
contextSentence: When those two things get conflated, you're listening into the wind.
contextSentenceKo: 이 두 가지가 뒤섞이면, 바람에 대고 듣는 것과 같습니다.

definition: An important quality or feature on which a particular thing depends or is based; originally a stone forming the base of a corner of a building
etymology: From Middle English, compound of 'corner' + 'stone', referring to the first stone set in a building's foundation
rootBreakdown: corner (모서리) + stone (돌) → 건물의 기초가 되는 돌 → 핵심 기반
contextSentence: I'd like to suggest that there are four really powerful cornerstones,
contextSentenceKo: 네 가지 정말 강력한 초석이 있다고 제안하고 싶습니다.

definition: The quality of being genuine, real, or true to one's own personality and values
etymology: From Greek 'authentikos' (original, genuine), from 'authentes' (one acting on one's own authority)
rootBreakdown: auto- (스스로) + hentes (행하는 자) → 자신에게 진실한 것
contextSentence: The A is authenticity, just being yourself.
contextSentenceKo: A는 진정성(authenticity), 그냥 자기 자신이 되는 것입니다.

definition: The quality of being honest and having strong moral principles; the state of being whole and undivided
etymology: From Latin 'integritas' (wholeness, completeness), from 'integer' (whole, complete)
rootBreakdown: in- (부정 접두사 아님, '안에') + teger (만지다/온전한) → 온전한 상태
contextSentence: The I is integrity, being your word, actually doing what you say,
contextSentenceKo: I는 성실함(integrity), 말한 것을 지키는 것, 실제로 말한 대로 행동하는 것,

definition: Including or considering all elements or aspects; fully comprehensive
etymology: From Latin 'exhaurire' (to drain out), from 'ex-' (out) + 'haurire' (to draw water)
rootBreakdown: ex- (밖으로) + haust (퍼내다) + -ive (형용사) → 모두 퍼내어 다 다룬
contextSentence: I'm not pretending this is an exhaustive list,
contextSentenceKo: 이것이 완전한 목록이라고 주장하는 것은 아닙니다만,

definition: Last but one in a series; second to the last
etymology: From Latin 'paenultimus', from 'paene' (almost) + 'ultimus' (last)
contextSentence: Penultimate, the six of the seven. Embroidery.
contextSentenceKo: 끝에서 두 번째, 일곱 중 여섯 번째. 윤색입니다.

definition: The art of decorating with needlework; figuratively, the addition of fictitious details to make a story more interesting
etymology: From Anglo-French 'enbrouderie', from 'enbrouder' (to embroider)
contextSentence: Penultimate, the six of the seven. Embroidery.
contextSentenceKo: 끝에서 두 번째, 일곱 중 여섯 번째. 윤색입니다.

definition: To cause a severe loss in the dignity of and respect for someone or something
etymology: From 'de-' (down) + 'mean' (in the sense of lowly), modeled on 'debase'
contextSentence: Exaggeration. It demeans our language, actually, sometimes.
contextSentenceKo: 과장. 사실 이것은 때때로 우리의 언어를 격하시킵니다.

definition: To praise enthusiastically and publicly; enthusiastic approval or praise
etymology: From Latin 'acclamare' (to shout at), from 'ad-' (to) + 'clamare' (to shout)
rootBreakdown: ac- (향하여) + claim (외치다) → 향하여 외치다 → 찬사를 보내다
contextSentence: I'm talking about this definition, to greet or acclaim enthusiastically,
contextSentenceKo: 이 정의를 말하는 겁니다. 열정적으로 환영하거나 찬사를 보내다,

definition: To search unsystematically and untidily through a mass or receptacle
etymology: From French 'arrumage' (arrangement of cargo), originally a nautical term for stowing cargo in a ship's hold
contextSentence: I'd like to have a little rummage in there with you now.
contextSentenceKo: 지금 여러분과 함께 그 안을 좀 뒤져보고 싶습니다.

definition: (In voice/music) The range of tones produced by a particular part of the vocal mechanism; a particular level of pitch
etymology: From Medieval Latin 'registrum' (list, catalog), from Latin 'regesta' (things recorded)
rootBreakdown: re- (다시) + gest (나르다/기록하다) + -er → 음악에서는 소리의 범위를 뜻함
contextSentence: Which will increase the power of your speaking. Register, for example.
contextSentenceKo: 이것들이 여러분의 말하기 힘을 높여줄 것입니다. 예를 들어, 음역대입니다.

definition: The character or quality of a musical sound or voice as distinct from its pitch and intensity
etymology: From French 'timbre' (stamp, character), from Medieval Greek 'tymbanon' (drum)
contextSentence: That's register. And we have timbre.
contextSentenceKo: 그것이 음역대입니다. 그리고 음색이 있습니다.

definition: The patterns of rhythm, stress, and intonation in a language; the musicality of speech
etymology: From Latin 'prosodia', from Greek 'prosoidia' (song sung to music, accent), from 'pros-' (to) + 'oide' (song)
contextSentence: Then prosody. I love prosody. This is the sing song, the meta language that we use in order to impart meaning.
contextSentenceKo: 그 다음은 운율입니다. 저는 운율을 좋아합니다. 의미를 전달하기 위해 사용하는 노래하듯한 리듬, 메타 언어입니다.

definition: Having a single unvaried tone; lacking in variety and interest; tediously uniform
meaningKo: 단조로운, 변화 없는, 한 음으로만 된
etymology: From Greek 'monotonos', from 'mono-' (single) + 'tonos' (tone, pitch)
contextSentence: That's where the word monotonic comes from or monotonous, monotone.
contextSentenceKo: 거기서 단조로운이라는 뜻의 monotonic, monotonous, monotone이라는 단어가 나옵니다.

definition: To make information known; to communicate or transmit knowledge, qualities, or feelings
etymology: From Latin 'impartire' (to share, divide), from 'in-' (into) + 'partire' (to divide, share)
contextSentence: This is the sing song, the meta language that we use in order to impart meaning.
contextSentenceKo: 의미를 전달하기 위해 사용하는 노래하듯한 리듬, 메타 언어입니다.

definition: To moderate or restrain; to soften or tone down the force of something
etymology: From Latin 'temperare' (to observe proper measure, moderate, restrain)
contextSentence: Tempered with love, of course, honesty is a great thing.
contextSentenceKo: 물론, 사랑으로 절제된 정직은 훌륭한 것입니다.

definition: The act of playing music or audio through a phone or speaker in a public place, imposing it on others
meaningKo: 공공장소에서 스피커로 소리를 틀어 다른 사람들에게 강요하는 행위
etymology: British slang portmanteau of 'sod' (British vulgar term for an annoying person) + 'broadcasting'
rootBreakdown: sod (짜증나는 사람) + casting (방송) → 무례하게 소리를 퍼뜨리는 행위
contextSentence: That's called sodcasting. Imposing your sound on people around you carelessly and inconsiderately.
contextSentenceKo: 그것을 '소드캐스팅'이라고 합니다. 주변 사람들에게 부주의하고 무신경하게 소리를 강요하는 것입니다.

definition: To attack continuously with questions, criticisms, or information; originally to attack with bombs or artillery
etymology: From French 'bombarder', from 'bombarde' (a type of cannon), ultimately from Latin 'bombus' (a buzzing sound)
contextSentence: You know, somebody is bombarding you with their opinions as if they were true.
contextSentenceKo: 누군가가 자신의 의견을 마치 사실인 것처럼 퍼붓는 거죠.
